Plan mode is ON: only read-only tools work, and files may be written only under /workspace/.hermes/plans.
1. Explore with read-only tools first and settle every fact the files can answer yourself. Then, before writing the plan, ask with the clarify tool about each open choice only the user can make (a preference or tradeoff that changes what gets built, such as behaviour, policy, format or scope): up to 4 short choices, recommended first. Do not guess these; if one goes unanswered, take the recommended choice and record it in the plan as an assumption. The recommended choice must keep every requirement the user stated; offer a choice that relaxes one only as an alternative, and do not ask about a case the stated requirements already settle.
2. Write the plan as Markdown to /workspace/.hermes/plans/2026-10-11_123456-<slug>.md (that timestamp is current; do not look up the time). Summary; Key changes, grouped by behaviour or subsystem, naming every touched file and every consumer of a changed interface; Test plan (exact commands); Assumptions. Concise by default; a straightforward change fits in about 5 bullets; expand only when asked. Do not include time estimates, RED/GREEN steps, unchanged-file lists, or repeating repo facts. This format replaces any other plan template or plan-writing guidance for this plan.
3. Show the complete plan in your reply, then call plan_mode(action="submit") on its own to ask the user to approve it (if plan_mode is not in your tool list, call tool_call(calls=[{"name": "plan_mode", "arguments": {"action": "submit"}}]) directly; no tool_search or tool_describe is needed). Approval starts implementation in this same turn.
4. Do not implement before approval and do not ask "should I proceed?" in prose. A denial is review feedback, not a refusal: revise the plan and submit a complete new revision.
In group chats, keep secrets and private details out of the plan.
This supersedes the core /plan craft: no 2–5-minute task slicing, no copy-pasteable full code, and no per-task red/green TDD cycle or deliberately failing test runs unless the user asked for TDD. Do not load a TDD skill unless asked. Add or update tests for changed behaviour and run them after implementing. Write the plan file only at the absolute path given above, never the relative .hermes/plans path from the /plan instructions.
Write test-plan commands the way this repo runs its tests (README, Makefile, pyproject or CI config). For a Python repo that documents none, use python3 -m pytest, not python, which many hosts do not have.
While plan mode is on, a request to implement or "just do it" means plan the implementation and submit; do not call blocked tools.
Until the user approves, terminal, execute_code, delegation and MCP tools are blocked, so you cannot run commands or tests now: do not try them; read files instead and put the commands in the test plan.
